entries.construction: UserGuide2017 p. 62 explicitly identifies the Release 2 revision: ER34651 individual and ER71571 family cross-sectional weights include the NIS-2017 sample. The staged February 2019 construction report excludes post-1997 immigrants from its ACS calibration population; the currently served official report is byte-identical. The June 2026 report on the 2023 cross-sectional weights documents the 2017 population control (ACS one-year PUMS, CPS not used, donut-hole families and group-quarters post-1997 immigrants excluded from the 2017 ACS estimate) and a calibration-variable selection approach used since 2017. The release chronology is documented, with a Release 2 versus Release 3 conflict; the 2017 base weights and raking dimensions matching the revised ER34651 remain unresolved.
entries.question: Which PSID document describes the construction of the revised 2017 individual cross-sectional weight ER34651, which now includes the 2017 Immigrant (NIS-2017) sample? In particular, how were base weights formed for the 2017 Immigrant sample, whose 2017 longitudinal family weight is zero, and combined with the core weights? And which calibration (raking) variables, interactions and trimming settings were used for 2017? The April 2021 and June 2026 cross-sectional reports document the 2017 population control and the calibration-variable selection approach, not these; the February 2019 construction report predates the revision. Do not remove immigrants to match the older report. Independent adjudication: A (genuinely ambiguous); needs u2-draft-4 amendment 6, pending Max's ruling (EV/phase2-20260927/out/u2-adjudicate.md line 129).
entries.part_b_finding: PARTIAL (u2-m1b Part B, revised 2026-09-29 after the independent review; docs/design/u2_m1b_psid_research.md section 3). The June 2026 report on the 2023 cross-sectional weights (tests/data/track_u2/psid_sources/cross_sec_weights_23.pdf) names ER34651 as the 2017 individual weight (Table A3, PDF p. 14); prints the 2017 sum of the individual weights beside the ACS one-year PUMS population total, with the CPS column 'Not Used' (Table A2, PDF p. 13); says that donut-hole families and post-1997 immigrants living in group quarters 'were excluded from the ACS estimate in 2017' (Table A2 note); and says PSID 'started to use a different approach to select the calibration variables since 2017' (PDF p. 6). The April 2021 report on the 2019 cross-sectional weights (tests/data/track_u2/psid_docs/cross_sec_weights_19.pdf) already documented the same 2017 control (Table A2a, PDF p. 17; Table A3, PDF p. 18; calibration approach 'since 2017', PDF p. 7). The May 2019 release notes say the weights for the 2017 Immigrant individuals 'remain zero and will be updated in Release 3', while UserGuide2017 PDF p. 62 dates the update to Release 2, an unresolved release-number conflict. Not documented online: the 2017 base weights, in particular for the 2017 Immigrant sample, and the 2017 raking dimensions.
